   session on shared directories and should have asked who else was working them before acting. My

   evidence of safety I would have deleted on no evidence at all. Same shape as the argv-ignoring
   validator earlier the same day: a check that RAN is not a check that could have come out the other
   way. A zero-denominator result must be treated as NO RESULT.

IMPORTANT CORRECTION to the earlier notes on this issue: the first diagnosis
(mosh's UDP data channel blocked by Framework's firewall, commit 8fe0796) was
WRONG -- a false signal from a broken local test harness. Every one of my
earlier live mosh reproductions ran through a pty with 0x0 window size
(script -q /dev/null with no controlling terminal), which crashes mosh's own
client internally (a std::vector::at() out-of-range exception while parsing
terminal dimensions) BEFORE it gets a real chance to attempt the UDP
handshake -- and that crash happens to print a misleading "did not make a
successful connection" message on its way out. Re-tested with a correctly
sized pty (80x24, via Python's pty module with an explicit TIOCSWINSZ ioctl)
and mosh connects to Framework cleanly on the first try. UDP was never
actually blocked. The two firewall changes made on Framework this session
(opening 60000-61000/udp in the default zone, then correctly assigning
tailscale0 to the trusted zone) are harmless and arguably still good
practice, but neither was the actual fix -- confirmed by re-testing mosh
after each and seeing the identical (fake) failure both times, using the
same flawed test harness. Apologies for the wasted round trip on the user's
end running those firewall commands.

REAL ROOT CAUSE (found by testing the ACTUAL remote_cmd ai-cli constructs,
not just a bare echo, through the corrected pty): ai-cli hardcoded
"zsh -l -c <remote_cmd>" as the interpreter run ON THE REMOTE HOST, in three
places in src/ai_cli/main.py -- the mosh_args remote command, the ssh_args
remote command, and the named-session allocation preflight
(_request_remote_session_allocation). Framework (Fedora) does not have zsh
installed at all -- confirmed directly via SSH (`which zsh` -> not found,
`rpm -q zsh` -> "package zsh is not installed", default login shell is
/usr/bin/bash). mosh-server's own execvp of the literal string "zsh" fails
instantly ("mosh-server: execvp: zsh: No such file or directory"), and
mosh's terminal-restore erases that exact diagnostic before printing
"[mosh is exiting.]" -- which is exactly, precisely what the user saw, with
no visible explanation.

FIX (systemic, per the user's explicit requirement -- works for any remote
machine, not a one-off Framework patch): added _resolve_remote_shell(), which
probes the remote host for its own available login shell (checks zsh first,
then bash, matching the existing SESSION_SHELL_PREFERENCE precedent already
used for local session launches in session_script.py) before constructing
any of the three remote commands, instead of assuming zsh exists everywhere.
The probe command itself is run via SSH's own default-shell dispatch, so it
makes no zsh assumption either. Falls back to "bash" on any probe failure
(unreachable host, timeout) so a genuine connectivity problem still surfaces
through the normal mosh/ssh retry path rather than failing inside the probe
itself. Also added -o ConnectTimeout=10 to the shared preflight SSH args so
neither the probe nor the existing named-session allocation call can hang
indefinitely on an unreachable host.
